name: Intent evolution: the most likely option or a checkable experiment
purpose: One balanced number (accuracy, cost and time, weights fixed in esoi.toml before any arm is scored) over Quest quests with experiments and outcomes: the reply proposes the option most likely to work with a metric that checks it, or an experiment when the best option is unknown, without nagging. The balance is the one number at every stage; the stages differ only in fidelity.
record: The balanced score of each implementation on the same Quest cases, one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Quest cases with a known outcome are few, so the rated first stage carries most of the early signal until real quests accumulate.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=an arm runs the whole Quest case set with no model call] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real quest case runs end to end and is hand-read]

name: Quest Consciousness on Quest cases
purpose: One balanced number over Quest cases for the composition of the five Consciousness records (Quest Requests, Quest Representatives, Quest Decision Requests, Feedback Learning and Intent Evolution), built on the hub's metric-the-consciousness and run on Quest-only cases.
record: The balanced score of the composition on the same Quest cases, one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: It scores nothing until the Quest case source is wired and the hub's metric is named in a builds_on table with its component.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the composition runs the whole Quest case set with no model call] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real Quest case runs end to end through the five Consciousness records and is hand-read]

name: Quest's work in the order Quest's rules give
purpose: The work that competes for a person's attention comes back in the order Quest's own rules give, in three uses of Prioritization: the standing work the autopilot starts (open asks before goals before ideas, the shorter goal horizon first, then the nearest deadline: the hub's rules with Quest's added), the asks put to the person (the overdue and nearer deadline first, the undated newest first, open asks oldest first) and the person's goals (their own rank first with the creator's legacy rank counting only for the creator, completed goals last). One balanced number (accuracy, cost and time, weights fixed in esoi.toml before any arm is scored) over the hub's Prioritization cases and Quest's own.
record: BUILDS ON the hub's prioritization metric (esoi.toml [builds_on.order_quest_work.hub_cases], half of the number): the hub's invented, neutral cases each exercise one generic rule and are not copied here; an arm answers all of them and inherits the hub's gates, and Quest's cases add only Quest's own rules. Quest's own twenty cases carry the other half, each tagged with its use (work, asks or goals), for goals with its level (quest, solution milestone, period goal, the day's tasks) and with the Quest test or rule it came from (a quest list with a person's rank map, the autopilot's order of asks, goals and ideas, the goal horizons and ladder, open asks oldest first, the asks-for-you digest order, goals by deadline with completed last, solutions by milestone and metric age, a period goal with no metric value as its milestone, the day's goals with the AI rep's last). The day's scheduling (time blocks, sustained focus) has no Quest rule or case yet, so none is scored. Accuracy is the share of cases whose whole order equals the reviewed order, balanced with cost and time by [balance.order_quest_work]; mean pairwise agreement is in the details. The expected orders were written by hand from the rules, never by an arm. The number is not split by use: a use that fails lowers the same number.
disadvantages: Twenty Quest cases, each taken from one Quest test or rule, so an ordering that only a live quest's data shows is not measured; whether the order is the one a person would choose is not scored, only that Quest's written rules are followed. The daily-task level has one case; how a day is scheduled for sustained focus is unmeasured until Quest has a written rule to take cases from.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the Quest arm and the hub's arms ran the same cases]
command: esoi run order_quest_work --impl quest_ordering; esoi run order_quest_work --impl hub_stated_fields; esoi run order_quest_work --impl hub_as_given
